sanskrit: ugrānnaṃ garhitaṃ devi gaṇānnaṃ śrāddhasūtakam ghuṣṭānnaṃ naiva bhoktavyaṃ śūdrānnaṃ naiva karhi cit
english: The food of a cruel man is condemned, O goddess, as is the food of a horde, the food connected with a śrāddha or a birth-impurity. Food announced by a public crier must never be eaten, and a Śūdra's food never at all.

sanskrit: śūdrānnaṃ garhitaṃ devi devadevair mahātmabhiḥ pitāmahamukhotsṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇam iti me matiḥ
english: The food of a Śūdra is condemned, O goddess, by the great-souled gods of gods; uttered from the mouth of the Grandsire himself, this is authoritative — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: śūdrānnenāvaśeṣeṇa jaṭhare yo mriyeta vai āhitāgnis tathā yajvā sa śūdragatibhāg bhavet
english: He in whose belly a remnant of a Śūdra's food remains when he dies — though he be one who has kindled the sacred fires and offered sacrifices — shares the destiny of a Śūdra.

sanskrit: tena śūdrānnaśeṣeṇa brahmasthānād apākṛtaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ śūdratām eti nāsti tatra vicāraṇā
english: By that remnant of a Śūdra's food a Brāhmaṇa is cast down from the station of Brahman and becomes a Śūdra — of this there is no question.

sanskrit: yasyānnenāvaśeṣeṇa jaṭhare yo mriyeta vai tāṃ tāṃ yoniṃ vrajed vipro yasyānnam upajīvati
english: A Brāhmaṇa in whose belly a remnant of another's food remains when he dies, whose food he has lived upon, passes into that very womb.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇatvaṃ śubhaṃ prāpya durlabhaṃ yo 'vamanyate abhojyānnāni cāśnāti sa dvijatvāt pateta vai
english: He who, having attained the auspicious and hard-won state of a Brāhmaṇa, holds it in contempt and eats forbidden food, surely falls from his twice-born estate.

sanskrit: surāpo brahmahā kṣudraś cauro bhagnavrato 'śuciḥ svādhyāyavarjitaḥ pāpo lubdho naikṛtikaḥ śaṭhaḥ
english: The drinker of liquor, the slayer of a Brāhmaṇa, the base man, the thief, the breaker of vows, the impure, he who has abandoned his sacred study, the sinful, the greedy, the deceitful, the crooked —

sanskrit: avratī vṛṣalībhartā kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī nihīnasevī vipro hi patati brahmayonitaḥ
english: the man without vows, the keeper of a Śūdra woman, the eater of an adulterer's food, the seller of Soma, the servant of the lowly — such a Brāhmaṇa falls from his Brahman-born nature.

sanskrit: gurutalpī gurudveṣī gurukutsāratiś ca yaḥ brahmadviṭ cāpi patati brāhmaṇo brahmayonitaḥ
english: He who defiles his teacher's bed, who hates his teacher, who delights in reviling his teacher, and who hates Brahman — such a Brāhmaṇa, too, falls from his Brahman-born nature.

sanskrit: ebhis tu karmabhir devi śubhair ācaritais tathā śūdro brāhmaṇatāṃ gacched vaiśyaḥ kṣatriyatāṃ vrajet
english: But by these auspicious deeds duly performed, O goddess, a Śūdra may attain Brāhmaṇahood, and a Vaiśya may attain Kṣatriyahood.

sanskrit: śūdrakarmāṇi sarvāṇi yathānyāyaṃ yathāvidhi śuśrūṣāṃ paricaryāṃ ca jyeṣṭhe varṇe prayatnataḥ kuryād avimanāḥ śūdraḥ satataṃ satpathe sthitaḥ
english: All the duties of a Śūdra, rightly and according to rule, with service and attendance upon the highest class — these let the Śūdra perform diligently and ungrudgingly, standing ever upon the good path.

sanskrit: daivatadvijasatkartā sarvātithyakṛtavrataḥ ṛtukālābhigāmī ca niyato niyatāśanaḥ
english: Honouring the gods and the twice-born, holding to the vow of hospitality toward all, approaching his wife only in season, self-restrained and temperate in food —

sanskrit: caukṣaś caukṣajanānveṣī śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ vṛthāmāṃsāny abhuñjānaḥ śūdro vaiśyatvam ṛcchati
english: clean and seeking the company of the clean, making his meal of the food that remains, never eating meat got in vain — such a Śūdra attains to Vaiśyahood.

sanskrit: ṛtavāg anahaṃvādī nirdvaṃdvaḥ śamakovidaḥ yajate nityayajñaiś ca svādhyāyaparamaḥ śuciḥ
english: Truthful in speech, free of self-assertion, beyond the pairs of opposites, skilled in tranquillity, performing the daily sacrifices, devoted above all to sacred study, and pure —

sanskrit: dānto brāhmaṇasatkartā sarvavarṇabubhūṣakaḥ gṛhasthavratam ātiṣṭhan dvikālakṛtabhojanaḥ
english: self-controlled, honouring Brāhmaṇas, wishing well to all the classes, holding to the householder's vow, taking food at the two appointed times —

sanskrit: śeṣāśī vijitāhāro niṣkāmo nirahaṃvadaḥ agnihotram upāsaṃś ca juhvānaś ca yathāvidhi
english: eating the remnant, having conquered his appetite, free of craving, free of self-assertion, tending the sacred fire and making oblations according to rule —

sanskrit: sarvātithyam upātiṣṭhañ śeṣānnakṛtabhojanaḥ tretāgnimantravihito vaiśyo bhavati vai yadi sa vaiśyaḥ kṣatriyakule śucau mahati jāyate
english: showing hospitality to all, making his meal of the food that remains, ordained to the three fires and their mantras — if a Vaiśya lives thus, he is born into a pure and great Kṣatriya family.

sanskrit: sa vaiśyaḥ kṣatriyo jāto janmaprabhṛti saṃskṛtaḥ upanīto vrataparo dvijo bhavati satkṛtaḥ
english: That Vaiśya, born now a Kṣatriya, sanctified from birth, invested with the sacred thread and devoted to his vows, becomes an honoured twice-born man.

sanskrit: dadāti yajate yajñaiḥ saṃskṛtair āptadakṣiṇaiḥ adhīte svargam anvicchaṃs tretāgniśaraṇaḥ sadā
english: He gives, he sacrifices with consecrated rites and ample fees, he studies, ever seeking heaven, taking refuge in the three fires.

sanskrit: ārtahastaprado nityaṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan satyaḥ satyāni kurute nityaṃ yaḥ sukhadarśanaḥ
english: Ever stretching out a giving hand to the afflicted, protecting his subjects by dharma, truthful, fulfilling his promises, and ever pleasant to behold —

sanskrit: dharmadaṇḍo na nirdaṇḍo dharmakāryānuśāsakaḥ yantritaḥ kāryakaraṇe ṣaḍbhāgakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
english: wielding the rod for justice and yet not without restraint, directing the works of dharma, governed in the discharge of his duties, taking the sixth part as his appointed due —

sanskrit: grāmyadharmān na seveta svacchandenārthakovidaḥ ṛtukāle tu dharmātmā patnīṃ seveta nityadā
english: let him not indulge the ways of carnal pleasure at his own whim, though skilled in worldly gain; rather, righteous in soul, let him approach his wife only in season.

sanskrit: sarvopavāsī niyataḥ svādhyāyaparamaḥ śuciḥ barhiṣkāntarite nityaṃ śayāno 'gnigṛhe sadā
english: Practising all the fasts, self-restrained, devoted above all to sacred study, pure, ever sleeping upon the strewn sacrificial grass within the fire-chamber —

sanskrit: sarvātithyaṃ trivargasya kurvāṇaḥ sumanāḥ sadā śūdrāṇāṃ cānnakāmānāṃ nityaṃ siddham iti bruvan
english: showing hospitality to the three classes with a gracious mind always, and ever saying to Śūdras who desire food, 'It is ready' —

sanskrit: svārthād vā yadi vā kāmān na kiṃ cid upalakṣayet pitṛdevātithikṛte sādhanaṃ kurute ca yaḥ
english: who notices nothing for his own gain or for his own desire, and who makes his every effort for the sake of the ancestors, the gods, and his guests —

sanskrit: svaveśmani yathānyāyam upāste bhaikṣam eva ca trikālam agnihotraṃ ca juhvāno vai yathāvidhi
english: who in his own house duly partakes even of alms, and who offers the fire-oblation thrice a day according to rule —

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ tretāgnimantrapūtaṃ vā samāviśya dvijo bhavet
english: and who, for the good of cows and Brāhmaṇas, is slain facing the foe in battle — or one purified by the three fires and their mantras — enters and becomes a twice-born man.

sanskrit: jñānavijñānasaṃpannaḥ saṃskṛto vedapāragaḥ vipro bhavati dharmātmā kṣatriyaḥ svena karmaṇā
english: Endowed with knowledge and discernment, sanctified, having mastered the Vedas, a righteous-souled Kṣatriya becomes a Brāhmaṇa by his own deeds.

sanskrit: etaiḥ karmaphalair devi nyūnajātikulodbhavaḥ śūdro 'py āgamasaṃpanno dvijo bhavati saṃskṛtaḥ
english: By these fruits of action, O goddess, even a Śūdra sprung from a lowly birth and family, if endowed with sacred learning and sanctified, becomes a twice-born man.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo vāpy asadvṛttaḥ sarvasaṃkarabhojanaḥ brāhmaṇyaṃ puṇyam utsṛjya śūdro bhavati tādṛśaḥ
english: And a Brāhmaṇa, too, of evil conduct, who eats every defiled mixture of food, casting off his holy Brāhmaṇahood, becomes such a one — a Śūdra.

sanskrit: karmabhiḥ śucibhir devi śuddhātmā vijitendriyaḥ śūdro 'pi dvijavat sevya iti brahmābravīt svayam
english: By pure deeds, O goddess, even a Śūdra of cleansed soul, his senses conquered, is to be honoured like a twice-born man — so Brahmā himself declared.

sanskrit: svabhāvakarma ca śubhaṃ yatra śūdre 'pi tiṣṭhati viśuddhaḥ sa dvijātir vai vijñeya iti me matiḥ
english: Where an auspicious nature and conduct dwell even in a Śūdra, that purified man is to be known indeed as twice-born — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: na yonir nāpi saṃskāro na śrutaṃ na ca saṃnatiḥ kāraṇāni dvijatvasya vṛttam eva tu kāraṇam
english: Neither birth, nor the sacraments, nor learning, nor lineage are the causes of being twice-born; conduct alone is the cause.

sanskrit: sarvo 'yaṃ brāhmaṇo loke vṛttena tu vidhīyate vṛtte sthitaś ca suśroṇi brāhmaṇatvaṃ nigacchati
english: Every Brāhmaṇa in this world is ordained such by his conduct; and one who stands firm in good conduct, O fair-hipped lady, attains to Brāhmaṇahood.

sanskrit: brāhmaḥ svabhāvaḥ kalyāṇi samaḥ sarvatra me matiḥ nirguṇaṃ nirmalaṃ brahma yatra tiṣṭhati sa dvijaḥ
english: The Brahman-nature, O blessed one, is the same everywhere — such is my conviction; where the qualityless, stainless Brahman abides, there is the twice-born man.

sanskrit: ete yoniphalā devi sthānabhāganidarśakāḥ svayaṃ ca varadenoktā brahmaṇā sṛjatā prajāḥ
english: These are the fruits of birth, O goddess, indicating one's portion and station, declared by the boon-granting Brahmā himself as he created creatures.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hi mahat kṣetraṃ loke carati pādavat yat tatra bījaṃ vapati sā kṛṣiḥ pāralaukikī
english: The Brāhmaṇa is a great field that moves about in the world on foot; the seed he sows there is the tillage that bears fruit in the world beyond.

sanskrit: mitāśinā sadā bhāvyaṃ satpathālambinā sadā brāhmamārgam atikramya vartitavyaṃ bubhūṣatā
english: He must ever be moderate in eating and ever cleave to the good path; one who wishes to flourish must not transgress, but conduct himself upon the way of Brahman.

sanskrit: saṃhitādhyāyinā bhāvyaṃ gṛhe vai gṛhamedhinā nityaṃ svādhyāyayuktena dānādhyayanajīvinā
english: As a householder in his home he must be a reciter of the sacred texts, ever given to study, living by giving and learning.

sanskrit: evaṃbhūto hi yo vipraḥ satataṃ satpathe sthitaḥ āhitāgnir adhīyāno brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: A Brāhmaṇa who is thus, standing ever upon the good path, having kindled the sacred fire and ever studying, becomes fit to be one with Brahman.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇyam eva saṃprāpya rakṣitavyaṃ yatātmabhiḥ yonipratigrahādānaiḥ karmabhiś ca śucismite
english: Having attained Brāhmaṇahood, it must be guarded by the self-restrained — guarded in marriage, in the acceptance of gifts, and in deeds, O lady of the bright smile.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yathā śūdro bhaved dvijaḥ brāhmaṇo vā cyuto dharmād yathā śūdratvam āpnute
english: All this I have told you — how a Śūdra may become twice-born, and how a Brāhmaṇa, fallen from dharma, comes to the state of a Śūdra.

sanskrit: umovāca bhagavan sarvabhūteśa surāsuranamaskṛta dharmādharme nṛṇāṃ deva brūhi me saṃśayaṃ vibho
english: Umā said: O Lord, ruler of all beings, worshipped by gods and demons, regarding the right and the wrong conduct of men, O god, resolve my doubt for me, O all-pervading one.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā trividhaṃ hi naraḥ sadā badhyate bandhanaiḥ pāśair mucyate 'py atha vā punaḥ
english: By deed, by thought, and by word — threefold — a man is ever bound by fetters and snares, or else is set free again.

sanskrit: kena śīlena vā deva karmaṇā kīdṛśena vā samācārair guṇair vākyaiḥ svargaṃ yāntīha mānavāḥ
english: By what character, O god, or by what kind of deed, by what conduct, what virtues, what words, do men attain heaven here?

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca devi dharmārthatattvajñe satyanitye dame rate sarvaprāṇihitaḥ praśnaḥ śrūyatāṃ buddhivardhanaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: O goddess, knower of the truth of dharma and artha, ever devoted to truth and to self-restraint — your question is for the welfare of all living beings; let it be heard, for it increases wisdom.

sanskrit: satyadharmaratāḥ santaḥ sarvalipsāvivarjitāḥ nādharmeṇa na dharmeṇa badhyante chinnasaṃśayāḥ
english: The good, devoted to truth and dharma, free of all craving, their doubts cut away, are bound neither by unrighteousness nor by righteousness.

sanskrit: pralayotpattitattvajñāḥ sarvajñāḥ samadarśinaḥ vītarāgā vimucyante puruṣāḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ
english: Those who know the truth of dissolution and origination, the all-knowing, the even-eyed, free of passion — such men are released from all bonds.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā ye na hiṃsanti kiṃ cana ye na sajjanti kasmiṃś cid badhyante te na karmabhiḥ
english: Those who by deed, thought, or word injure nothing whatever, who cling to nothing — they are not bound by their actions.

sanskrit: prāṇātipātād viratāḥ śīlavanto dayānvitāḥ tulyadveṣyapriyā dāntā mucyante karmabandhanaiḥ
english: Refraining from the destruction of life, virtuous, full of compassion, regarding the hated and the loved alike, self-controlled — they are freed from the bonds of action.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtadayāvanto viśvāsyāḥ sarvajantuṣu tyaktahiṃsāsamācārās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Compassionate toward all beings, trusted by every creature, who have renounced all violent conduct — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: parasve nirmamā nityaṃ paradāravivarjakāḥ dharmalabdhārthabhoktāras te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Free of all greed for another's wealth, ever shunning another's wife, enjoying only riches gained by righteous means — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: mātṛvat svasṛvac caiva nityaṃ duhitṛvac ca ye paradāreṣu vartante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who ever look upon other men's wives as upon a mother, a sister, or a daughter — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: stainyān nivṛttāḥ satataṃ saṃtuṣṭāḥ svadhanena ca svabhāgyāny upajīvanti te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who refrain ever from theft, content with their own wealth, and who live upon their own portion — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: svadāraniratā ye ca ṛtukālābhigāminaḥ agrāmyasukhabhogāś ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who are devoted to their own wives, approaching them only in season, and who do not give themselves to vulgar pleasures — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: paradāreṣu ye nityaṃ cāritrāvṛtalocanāḥ yatendriyāḥ śīlaparās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those whose eyes are ever veiled by virtue in the presence of other men's wives, restrained in their senses, devoted to good character — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa devakṛto mārgaḥ sevitavyaḥ sadā naraiḥ akaṣāyakṛtaś caiva mārgaḥ sevyaḥ sadā budhaiḥ
english: This is the path made by the gods, always to be followed by men; and the path freed of the taints of passion is ever to be followed by the wise.

sanskrit: dānadharmatapoyuktaḥ śīlaśaucadayātmakaḥ vṛttyarthaṃ dharmahetor vā sevitavyaḥ sadā naraiḥ svargavāsam abhīpsadbhir na sevyas tv ata uttaraḥ
english: Endowed with charity, righteousness, and austerity, made of good character, purity, and compassion — this path, whether for one's livelihood or for the sake of dharma, must ever be followed by men who long to dwell in heaven; but that which is beyond it should not be followed.

sanskrit: umovāca vācātha badhyate yena mucyate 'py atha vā punaḥ tāni karmāṇi me deva vada bhūtapate 'nagha
english: Umā said: Those deeds of speech by which a man is bound, or again is set free — tell me of them, O god, lord of beings, O sinless one.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca ātmahetoḥ parārthe vā narmahāsyāśrayāt tathā ye mṛṣā na vadantīha te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Maheśvara said: Those who, whether for their own sake or another's, or out of jest and laughter, never speak falsehood here — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: vṛttyarthaṃ dharmahetor vā kāmakārāt tathaiva ca anṛtaṃ ye na bhāṣante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who, whether for livelihood or for the sake of dharma, or even at the bidding of desire, do not utter untruth — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: ślakṣṇāṃ vāṇīṃ nirābādhāṃ madhurāṃ pāpavarjitām svāgatenābhibhāṣante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who address others with a smooth speech, free of harm, sweet, free of evil, and with words of welcome — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: kaṭukāṃ ye na bhāṣante paruṣāṃ niṣṭhurāṃ giram apaiśunyaratāḥ santas te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who never speak a bitter, harsh, or cruel word, the good who delight in the absence of slander — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: piśunāṃ ye na bhāṣante mitrabhedakarīṃ giram ṛtāṃ maitrīṃ prabhāṣante te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who never speak a slanderous word that sets friends at variance, but utter true and friendly speech — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: varjayanti sadā sūcyaṃ paradrohaṃ ca mānavāḥ sarvabhūtasamā dāntās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who ever shun tale-bearing and treachery against others, even toward all beings and self-controlled — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: śaṭhapralāpād viratā viruddhaparivarjakāḥ saumyapralāpino nityaṃ te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who refrain from deceitful prattle, who shun what is hostile, and who ever speak gently — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: na kopād vyāharante ye vācaṃ hṛdayadāraṇīm sāntvaṃ vadanti kruddhāpi te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who, even in anger, do not utter a speech that tears the heart, but speak conciliating words though provoked — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: eṣa vāṇīkṛto devi dharmaḥ sevyaḥ sadā naraiḥ śubhaḥ satyaguṇo nityaṃ varjanīyā mṛṣā budhaiḥ
english: This dharma wrought of speech, O goddess, auspicious and ever endowed with the quality of truth, is always to be followed by men; falsehood must ever be shunned by the wise.

sanskrit: umovāca manasā badhyate yena karmaṇā puruṣaḥ sadā tan me brūhi mahābhāga devadeva pinākadhṛk
english: Umā said: By what deed of the mind a man is ever bound — tell me that, O greatly blessed one, god of gods, wielder of the Pināka bow.

sanskrit: maheśvara uvāca mānaseneha dharmeṇa saṃyuktāḥ puruṣāḥ sadā svargaṃ gacchanti kalyāṇi tan me kīrtayataḥ śṛṇu
english: Maheśvara said: Men ever joined with the dharma of the mind go to heaven, O blessed one; hear it as I recount it to you.

sanskrit: duṣpraṇītena manasā duṣpraṇītatarākṛtiḥ badhyate mānavo yena śṛṇu cānyac chubhānane
english: By a mind ill-directed a man becomes of even more ill-directed form, and is bound by it; hear, moreover, of the other side, O fair-faced one.

sanskrit: araṇye vijane nyastaṃ parasvaṃ vīkṣya ye narāḥ manasāpi na hiṃsanti te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who, beholding another's wealth left in a forest or a lonely place, do not lay hold of it even in thought — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: grāme gṛhe vā yad dravyaṃ pārakyaṃ vijane sthitam nābhinandanti vai nityaṃ te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Whatever goods of another are left unguarded in a village or a house, those who never covet them — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: tathaiva paradārān ye kāmavṛttān rahogatān manasāpi na hiṃsanti te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: And those who, even toward another's wife given to passion and met in a secret place, do no harm even in thought — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: śatruṃ mitraṃ ca ye nityaṃ tulyena manasā narāḥ bhajanti maitrāḥ saṃgamya te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those men who ever regard foe and friend with an equal mind, and meeting them deal with both in friendship — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: śrutavanto dayāvantaḥ śucayaḥ satyasaṃgarāḥ svair arthaiḥ parisaṃtuṣṭās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Learned, compassionate, pure, true to their pledges, fully content with their own wealth — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: avairā ye tv anāyāsā maitracittaparāḥ sadā sarvabhūtadayāvantas te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Those who bear no enmity, are free of agitation, ever devoted to a friendly mind, compassionate toward all beings — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: śraddhāvanto dayāvantaś cokṣāś cokṣajanapriyāḥ dharmādharmavido nityaṃ te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Full of faith, compassionate, clean and dear to clean folk, ever knowing right from wrong — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: śubhānām aśubhānāṃ ca karmaṇāṃ phalasaṃcaye vipākajñāś ca ye devi te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: And those who know the ripening of the gathered fruits of deeds both good and evil, O goddess — those men go to heaven.

sanskrit: nyāyopetā guṇopetā devadvijaparāḥ sadā samatāṃ samanuprāptās te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ
english: Endowed with justice, endowed with virtue, ever devoted to the gods and the twice-born, having attained to equanimity — those men go to heaven.
